pr_title: colexec: plan CAST operator for CASE arms when types are mismatched
pr_body:
CASE operator has predefined output type that all THEN arms as well as
the ELSE arm must respect. However, we also allow for comparable types
to be output. This caused a type conversion error in the vectorized
engine and is now fixed by planning an explicit (although internal) CAST
to the desired output type (when needed).

Fixes: #43550.

Release note (bug fix): Previously, an internal error could occur when
CASE operator operating on distinct although compatible types was
executed via the vectorized engine, and now this is fixed. For example,
a query similar to 'SELECT CASE WHEN false THEN 0:::INT2 ELSE 1:::INT8 END'
previously would error out.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/43557)
I was just wondering if there was a codepath I missed which is why we needed to return err, thats all

issue_context.title: colexec: incorrect type assumptions of CASE operator in some cases
issue_context.body:
Extracted from https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/43457#issuecomment-569002516

The following interaction
```
root@:26257/defaultdb> create table t(a int2 primary key);
CREATE TABLE

Time: 4.583ms

root@:26257/defaultdb> insert into t values (1);
INSERT 1

Time: 4.326ms

root@:26257/defaultdb> set vectorize_row_count_threshold=0;
SET

Time: 467µs

root@:26257/defaultdb> select case when a = 0 then a else 1:::INT8 end from t;
```
produces an internal error:
```
ERROR: internal error: unexpected error from the vectorized runtime: interface conversion: coldata.column is []int64, not []int16
SQLSTATE: XX000
DETAIL: stack trace:
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/execerror/error.go:70: func1()
runtime/panic.go:679: gopanic()
runtime/iface.go:255: panicdottypeE()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/col/coldata/vec.go:194: Int16()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/col/coldata/vec.eg.go:501: Copy()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/allocator.go:118: func1()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/allocator.go:90: performOperation()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/allocator.go:118: Copy()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/case.go:204: Next()
...
```
The problem here is that `CASE` operator has the output column with type `INT2`, but in `ELSE` case we explicitly asked for conversion to `INT8`. The output of `EXPLAIN (TYPES)` shows that `INT2` output type is expected.

Here is `EXPLAIN (VEC)`:
```
  └ Node 1                                
    └ *colexec.caseOp                     
      ├ *colexec.bufferOp                 
      │ └ *colexec.colBatchScan           
      ├ *colexec.projEQInt16Int64ConstOp  
      │ └ *colexec.bufferOp               
      └ *colexec.constInt64Op             
        └ *colexec.bufferOp
```

I'm actually not quite sure what is the correct way to fix this. Possibly we could plan casts to the case's output type in all `WHEN` and `ELSE` arms (when needed). cc @jordanlewis thoughts?
comments:
Yeah, we will need to plan casts for now. Really the optimizer/typechecker should be doing this though.

In general, CASE should require that all arms have the same output type. That includes width. cc @otan - this is related to the type system overhaul. We correctly constrain CASE outputs to be the same type family, but really we need the outputs to be identical in other attributes as well, like width.

review_comments: nit, but why is this changed?
